summary: Bettina Bäumer is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at the University of Salzburg and under Lakshman Joo (1986). She served as Director of the Alice Boner Institute (~1989) and Professor at the University of Vienna (~1997).

Bettine Birge works in sinology and history/archaeology. She completed her Ph.D. at Columbia University under William Theodore de Bary, taught Di Luo, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann (1888–1961) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Kiel (~1907–1908), and Bonn (~1909–1912), and later held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1923–1933), SOAS University of London (~1936–1945), Kiel, and Hamburg.

Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. A teacher of Surendra Man Bajracharya, he has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti (1928–2012) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at Osmania University (~1962–1986) and held a post at the Institute for Advanced Study (~1999–2000).

Bhagavan Das (1869–1958) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta and served as Honorary Secretary of the Board of Trustees and Managing Committee at Central Hindu College (~1898–1914).

Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he is attested in 1976 and served as head of the Research Department by 1989.

Bhajagovinda Ghosh works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 1994, he was attested as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as an Editorial Board Member for the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi (master's), and Agra University (linguistics doctorate), and held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Bhikkhu Bodhi, earned a PhD from the University of Ceylon, and habilitated at the University of Marburg. He held posts at Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy and Hamburg.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Brooklyn College, Claremont Graduate University (PhD), and under Nyanaponika Thera and Balangoda Ananda Maitreya. He was an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984) and founded Buddhist Global Relief.

Bhikkhu Pāsādika works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Magadh University and held posts at the University of Kassel, the University of Bergen, and the University of Marburg, where he was a professor (~1993).

Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She has held posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College, where she was attested as an Assistant Researcher in 2012, and at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Bhuvan Chandel is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She was a professor at Panjab University (attested 2003) and served as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~2003–2007).

Bimal Krishna Matilal (1935–1991) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Calcutta and Harvard under W.V.O. Quine and Dagfinn Føllesdal. He founded the Journal of Indian Philosophy and became Spalding Professor at Oxford in 1976.

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha (1919–2002) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of London. He was a long-time professor at Patna University and Hon. Joint Director of Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute.

Bing Chen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He became a professor at Sichuan University around 1987 and was attested as a professor at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences in 1993.

Bintao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Ma completed an MA at Peking University in 2008 and earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xueyu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha (1894–1961) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and Harvard University, and worked as an Anthropologist at the Zoological Survey of India (~1927–1945).

Birgit Kellner works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She earned her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura, served as a professor at the University of Vienna, and heads the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
